target_customer: Operators of EV and autonomous vehicle fleet depots, ports and logistics yards
problem: Depot charging labor costs about $900k per depot per year, downtime costs up to $650k, and building new depots costs $8M+ and takes 2 to 3 years (company figures).
business_model: Robotic charging and inspection systems sold or leased to fleet depots; pricing not public
product_category: Robotics, autonomous depot charging and inspection

founders.name: Celine Wang
education: Stanford, BS and MS Mechanical Engineering

competitors.name: Rocsys
competitors.what: Robotic plug-in charging; M1 multi-bay system for robotaxi depots

competitors.name: Electrify America with Stable
competitors.what: Robotic fast charging facility for self driving fleets

competitors.name: Siemens Depot360
competitors.what: Charging as a service platform for commercial fleets

technical_complexity.rationale: Vision guided plug insertion across many vehicle types and connectors, with reliability needed in outdoor depots.

defensibility.rationale: Closed loop data per charge event helps, but several funded charging robot makers and OEM prototypes exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rocsys raised and launched a multi bay product aimed at the same robotaxi depot wedge.

market_need_then: Robotaxi and EV fleet growth strained depot labor, and one analysis cites one human per 12 to 14 vehicles for charging and maintenance.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and industrial: 'Manual charging breaks at scale.'

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that fits the product; the branding search found no brand press, only directory and profile pages.

outcome_analysis: RoboDock is an active early robotics company from founders with Zipline, Amazon and Plus experience. It has a public launch in March 2026 but no named customers or confirmed financing. A funded competitor, Rocsys, targets the same depot wedge, so pilot wins are the next milestone.
notes: CB Insights shows a $500K convertible note on 2026-02-01 from Y Combinator; PitBook shows a seed round dated 2026-03-24 and an accelerator deal 2026-01-09 with investors Founder Factor, Sovereign's Capital, Team Ignite Ventures. These are aggregator figures that conflict on labels and dates, so no round is recorded. Team size listed as 2, 3 and 4 across sources. Competitors Rocsys 2026 items postdate the batch start and show the market, not what existed at founding.
